learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing, within its field of application.
Develop the ability to work in a team.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and permanent training.
That the student develops skills and techniques for solving problems of mechanisms and machines.
That the student knows basic techniques for the synthesis of mechanisms.
That the student knows computer tools for the analysis of mechanisms.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the theory of Machines and Mechanisms
Static and dynamic analysis of Machines
Graphical analysis of velocities in Mechanisms
Graphical analysis of accelerations in Mechanisms
teaching_methods: Practical classes with kinematic simulation of mechanisms and report preparation

assessment_methods.method: Test of static and dynamic analysis of Machines, composed of theoretical questions and/or practical problems.
Test of kinematic analysis of Mechanisms by analytical methods, composed of theoretical questions and/or practical problems.
Test of graphical analysis of velocities and accelerations in Mechanisms, composed of theoretical questions and/or practical problems.
Test of graphical synthesis of Mechanisms, composed of theoretical questions and/or practical problems.

assessment_rules: The ordinary evaluation consists of four tests. Each test requires a minimum score of 4 out of 10. The weighting of each test is the same for both the first and second calls. For exceptional evaluation, the system consists of 4 tests with the same content and weights as the ordinary evaluation, also requiring a minimum of 4 points out of 10 for each test.
